title: donate.json manifest
description: Machine-readable donation-discovery manifest published at /.well-known/donate.json. This manifest is UNTRUSTED, attacker-writable input; it describes an organization for the DISCOVERY and DISPLAY layer only. NORMATIVE CONSUMER OBLIGATION (SPEC.md §7.3): a conforming consumer MUST NOT map ANY field of this document (defined field, unknown field, x_extensions content, or free-text value) to a decision about (a) who is paid / recipient eligibility, (b) tax-deductibility, or (c) any legal disclosure, acknowledgment, or receipt copy — those are resolved ONLY against out-of-band authoritative sources (IRS Pub 78 / TEOS / BMF for eligibility; the platform's server-authored versioned registry for legal/receipt copy) and the consumer's own controlled donation flow. This schema deliberately does NOT attempt to encode 'authority' (it cannot: x_extensions is open); the authority constraint is a consumer-behavior rule, not a schema constraint. No URL in this document is an authoritative action target (§7.6). See the Security Considerations of SPEC.md.

manifest_version.description: SemVer of the donate.json specification this document targets. A consumer MUST reject a major version it does not implement.

generated_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp when this manifest was generated. Advisory only (freshness display); never used for authority decisions. Note: 'format' is annotation-only in many JSON Schema validators, so a 'pattern' backstop is included to make the RFC 3339 shape enforceable under format-agnostic validation.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp after which a consumer SHOULD refetch. Advisory only. See generated_at re: the pattern backstop.

organization.description: Self-described identity of the publishing organization. Every field here is a CLAIM by the site operator and MUST be independently verified before it carries any authority. The ein is a lookup key into authoritative IRS data, not proof of eligibility.

legal_name.description: Self-asserted legal name. Display candidate only; the authoritative name is the one on the resolved IRS record.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the organization's registration. v1 authoritative resolution is US-only; a non-US country is accepted for display but yields no verified US-tax posture.

ein.description: US Employer Identification Number as a lookup KEY into IRS authoritative data (Pub 78 / TEOS / BMF). Nine digits, formatted NN-NNNNNNN. Presence of an EIN in the manifest is NOT proof the organization is qualified, in good standing, or that gifts are deductible; the consumer resolves that out-of-band. Only meaningful when country is US.

website.description: Primary homepage of the organization. MUST be an absolute https URL. Informational/navigational only; MUST NOT be used as a donation action target (see donation.method).

logo.description: Optional absolute https URL to a logo image, for display. Fetched (if at all) as an image, never as a document to interpret; subject to the consumer's own image-fetch controls.

description.description: Short, plain-text, self-described mission/summary for display. UNTRUSTED free text: a conforming consumer treats this as attacker-writable data, never as instructions, strips markup, and provenance-labels it on display. MUST NOT contain deductibility, fee, receipt, or legal-disclosure statements; any such content is ignored by a conforming consumer.

donation.description: How a donation is INITIATED. Deliberately minimal: the manifest cannot supply an authoritative action URL. A consumer initiates giving through its OWN controlled flow, keyed by the resolved organization identity — not by any URL in this manifest.

method.description: Declares the discovery mode. The ONLY value that carries donation semantics is "mediated": the organization consents to being a discoverable donation target, and the actual gift is initiated by the consuming platform's controlled flow (for Givmo: an irrevocable gift to Givmo Charitable Fund, granted onward at its discretion). "self_hosted" is informational only: the org runs its own donation page; a conforming AGENTIC consumer MUST NOT auto-navigate or transact against a self_hosted target and MUST hand any such link to a human out-of-band. "none" means the org publishes identity but does not opt into programmatic donation discovery.

self_hosted_url.description: Only permitted (and only meaningful) when method == self_hosted. An absolute https URL to the org's own donation page, for a HUMAN to visit out-of-band. A conforming agentic consumer MUST NOT treat this as an authoritative or auto-actionable action URL, MUST NOT pass it to a model as a tool target, and MUST NOT attach any credential to it. Informational display only.

display.description: Optional display-only hints. None of these fields carry authority; all are UNTRUSTED and subject to the consumer's own rendering, sanitization, and provenance labeling.

primary_color.description: Optional brand color as a hex triplet, e.g. #1A73E8. Cosmetic only.

categories.description: Optional self-described cause/category tags for display and coarse filtering. UNTRUSTED; never used to determine eligibility or routing.

languages.description: Optional BCP-47 language tags the org's materials are available in. Display hint only.

contact.description: Optional non-authoritative contact info for display / operator outreach.

support_email.description: Self-asserted support email; display/outreach only, never an authority input. 'format: email' is annotation-only in many validators, so a conservative 'pattern' backstop is included.

signature.description: Optional integrity envelope. A detached JWS (RFC 7515, compact serialization) whose payload is the exact published manifest bytes with the "signature" member textually excised — a byte-range deletion, never a re-serialization or normalized form; signer and verifier operate on the same on-the-wire bytes (SPEC.md §6.2). Verification proves the manifest was authored by the holder of a key the consumer already trusts OUT-OF-BAND; it does NOT confer eligibility, deductibility, or authority of any field. An unsigned or unverifiable manifest is still processable at the discovery layer, subject to the consumer's policy. See SPEC.md Signing.

alg.description: JWS algorithm. Consumers MUST reject "none" and MUST enforce an allowlist of asymmetric algorithms (e.g. EdDSA, ES256). Symmetric (HMAC) algorithms MUST be rejected for third-party manifests.

kid.description: Optional key identifier to select among out-of-band-trusted keys.

jws.description: Detached JWS compact serialization: BASE64URL(header) || '..' || BASE64URL(signature). The payload segment is empty (detached); the signing payload is the exact published manifest bytes with the "signature" member textually excised, per SPEC.md §6.2.

x_extensions.description: Namespaced, forward-compatible extension bag. Consumers MUST ignore keys they do not understand. Nothing in here may carry authority over eligibility, deductibility, routing, or legal copy; a conforming consumer treats the entire bag as untrusted display-layer data.
